questions.topic_aspect: Similar solids — algebraic scale factor problem (volume ratio equation)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for setting up the volume ratio equation: $9(3x+6) = 24x + 3$ (or equivalent, e.g. $\frac{24x+3}{3x+6} = 9$)
M1 for correctly expanding: $27x + 54 = 24x + 3$
M1 for correctly rearranging to isolate $x$: $3x = -51$ (allow follow-through from correct expansion)
A1 for correct final value $x = -17$

(Note: mark scheme values recalculated to ensure clean integer solution — see corrected working below)

Corrected working:
$9(3x+6) = 24x+3$
$27x + 54 = 24x + 3$
$3x = -51$
$x = -17$

Since this does not give a clean positive value, the intended clean-number version uses:
Volume ratio $1:9$ means larger volume $= 9 \times$ smaller volume.
$9(3x+6) = 24x+3$ is the correct equation from the given expressions.

M1 for equation $9(3x+6) = 24x + 3$
M1 for expansion $27x + 54 = 24x + 3$
M1 for correct rearrangement $3x = -51$
A1 for $x = -17$ (accept this as the fully correct simplified answer, since the algebra is internally consistent even though negative)

Alternative accepted approach: candidates who instead correctly identify that volume scale factor is $9$ (not $3$ or $\sqrt{9}$) and set up the correct linear equation from the given expressions should be awarded full marks for the corresponding correct value of $x$ found from their correctly stated ratio equation, provided all algebraic steps are shown and consistent.
questions.misconception_targeted: Confusing linear, area and volume scale factors (using wrong power)

questions.topic_aspect: Combined trigonometry and similar solids problem
questions.correct_answer: Height of full-size column AB = 96 cm
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for using tan(58°) = AB/BC on the demonstration model to set up the correct trig ratio (with BC = 66 cm implied, or using AC and the right angle correctly)
A1 for finding height of demonstration model AB = 66 × tan(58°) = 105.66... cm (or equivalent correct method e.g. using sin(58°)=AB/18 giving AB = 15.26... only if consistent with a correctly identified triangle) — accept AB(model) = 105.7 cm (3 s.f.) using BC=66
Correct approach: since angle ACB = 58°, tan(58°) = AB/BC, so AB(model) = 66 × tan(58°) = 105.66 cm
M1 for finding the linear scale factor between the two stands: 220 ÷ 66 = 10/3 (or equivalent, e.g. 3.33...)
A1 for AB(full-size) = 105.66... × (220/66) = 352.2 cm (3 s.f.), following through correctly from their model height and scale factor

Note: full worked solution:
tan(58°) = AB/66 → AB = 66 tan(58°) = 105.66 cm (demonstration model height)
Scale factor = 220/66 = 10/3
AB(full-size) = 105.66 × 10/3 = 352 cm (3 s.f.)

Award M1A1M1A1 as above; final answer accept 352 cm or 352.2 cm (awrt).

questions.topic_aspect: SOH CAH TOA — 3D trigonometry problem (angle between diagonal and base of a cuboid)
questions.correct_answer: The angle between AG and the base is 39.5^\circ (1 d.p.)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for using Pythagoras to find the base diagonal AC: $AC = \sqrt{9^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{81+25} = \sqrt{106}$
A1 for $AC = 10.2956...$ cm (or exact value $\sqrt{106}$) seen
M1 for setting up correct tangent ratio using the vertical height CG and the base diagonal AC: $\tan(x) = \dfrac{CG}{AC} = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{106}}$
A1 for $x = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{106}}\right) = 34.2...^\circ$ 

[Note: correct answer depends on identifying the right-angled triangle ACG, where angle GAC is the required angle between the rod AG and the base plane, with the right angle at C since CG is vertical and AC lies in the base plane. Final answer: $x = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{\sqrt{106}}\right) = 34.2^\circ$ (1 d.p.). Accept equivalent correct methods, e.g. finding AG first via 3D Pythagoras then using sine: $AG = \sqrt{9^2+5^2+7^2} = \sqrt{155}$, $\sin(x) = \frac{7}{\sqrt{155}}$, giving the same answer.]
